page: Microsoft Azure M8ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned via Microsoft Hyper-V. The configuration features an Intel Xeon Platinum 8280M processor operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 8 vCPUs derived from 4 dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled (2 threads per core). Cache allocation includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 105 MB of shared L3 cache. The CPU instruction set includes AVX and AVX-512 extensions alongside standard cryptographic (AES) and integer bit manipulation flags.

Hardware capacity is heavily skewed toward memory density, providing 219.0 GB of RAM, or 27.34 GB per vCPU. Local storage is supplied via a bundled 275 GB SSD. No GPUs are attached to this server type, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The high memory-to-core ratio allows massive datasets to reside fully in system memory without requiring a large allocation of compute cores.

Benchmark testing shows modest throughput across general compute and raw processing tasks. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 857.0 (bottom 10%) and a multi-core score of 3389.0 (bottom 25%). Stress-ng CPU tests yielded 1036.79 for single-core and 5448.42 for multi-core. In memory testing, cached 16 KB read-only bandwidth registered at 304.96 GB/sec, while uncached 256 MB read bandwidth settled at 36.63 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth reached 31.88 GB/sec. Specialized workloads such as small 135M LLM inference recorded average performance tier results of 423.6 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 83.59 tokens/sec for generation.

The primary operational tradeoff of the M8ms is low core execution speed relative to its immense memory footprint. Qualitative cost efficiency favors scenarios where massive working sets require large RAM pools but low concurrency and compute intensity. It is best aligned with large in-memory caching solutions, memory-bound enterprise database engines, and in-memory analytical workloads that do not demand high parallel CPU throughput.

The platform is defined by an extreme memory footprint, offering 219.0 GB of RAM alongside 275 GB of bundled local SSD storage. No dedicated GPUs are present. Benchmark results reflect low-to-moderate computational and compression performance, exemplified by Geekbench scores of 857.0 single-core and 3389.0 multi-core, alongside a multi-core stress-ng rating of 5448.42. Large-block write bandwidth reaches 31.88 GB/sec, balancing its lower compute throughput. The M8ms is targeted at memory-intensive enterprise tasks requiring minimal compute scaling, including in-memory databases, large cache layers, and memory-constrained analytical processing.
